Under NativeOutput constrained decoding the output size is governed by the compiled grammar/schema, so a 'be concise' instruction may not reduce it — the retries could burn the shared allowance without progress
findings.finding: The plan extends the concision-reclassification guard to the NativeOutput (constrained-decoding) branch — 'the NativeOutput branch runs as the same bounded operation ... sharing ... the concision guard' — turning a length/max_tokens truncation into a retryable 'Make your response as concise as possible' ModelRetry even under a FIXED decoding grammar, but does not reason through whether a concision reask can meaningfully shrink a constrained-decoded output (the schema/grammar, not verbosity, drives its size) or justify changing today's terminal treatment of a truncated native turn.
findings.location: Approach — 'NativeOutput preserved.' paragraph and item 2 (concision guard)
scenarios: A native-capable model truncates a large structured verdict at max_tokens; the guard reclassifies it as concision-retryable and re-runs the same constrained decode, which truncates again until the shared output allowance is exhausted, then aborts — spending N extra full requests where today it fast-failed after one.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restrict the concision reclassification to the PromptedOutput branch (leaving NativeOutput's length/max_tokens terminal per structured.check_response), or add an explicit rationale + acceptance case showing native concision-retry recovers rather than merely re-truncating and burning the shared allowance.

This is a design choice, not an incompatibility with S1's contract.
